package.name: cite_description
package.description:
L1: the project's own description assets, installed so that a `package://` or `file://$(find cite_description)` URI resolves to them.
This is charter §7's `cite_description`, created for the first thing that needed it: the convex-hull collision meshes ADR-0028 decides on. It holds no code and no node.
ADMISSION TEST, in the style ADR-0034 and ADR-0040 set for the two packages that came before it, because a package named for a layer will otherwise accumulate whatever that layer touched. Something belongs here only if all three hold:
1. it is GEOMETRY OR MATERIAL a simulator or a planner loads by URI — a mesh, a material, a texture — and not configuration, code or data; 2. it is OURS: authored here, or DERIVED here from a pinned dependency. Third-party geometry is imported by `external/cite.repos` and never copied into this tree (ADR-0008); 3. it is NOT generated from the L0 facility model. Everything that is lives in `cite_generated`, whole, and is diffed against a fresh generator run (ADR-0021). A hull is derived from a VENDOR MESH rather than from the model, and `./scripts/validate-model` must keep running on a machine that has no vendor checkout — which is exactly why the two are separate packages rather than one.
WHAT IT INSTALLS AND WHERE THAT COMES FROM. The files live in `assets/` at the repository root, where ADR-0012's storage policy puts simulator assets and where ADR-0028 says hulls go. This package installs that directory rather than holding a second copy of it, so `assets/` stays the one place an asset lives and this package stays the one place an asset is installed from.
